mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Certificate of Registered Corporation Information
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court having jurisdiction over the Company's registered office in the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: issue official court registry certificate and obtain Apostille certificate from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) of the Republic of Korea. Consular Legalization path: issue official court registry certificate, authenticate it at MOFA, and present it to the destination country's embassy or consulate in Seoul. Use only one path depending on whether the destination state is party to the Hague Apostille Convention; do not combine Apostille and consular legalization in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Registered Particulars
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO) / competent District Court registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: registry-issued certificate authenticated by MOFA Apostille certificate. Consular Legalization path: registry-issued certificate authenticated by MOFA and legalized by the destination state embassy/consulate in Seoul. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing officers and bank account signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of KR_YUHANGHOESA (Yuhan Hoesa LLC) certified by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarize the resolution/PoA in the Republic of Korea and obtain MOFA Apostille. Consular Legalization path: notarize in Korea, authenticate at MOFA, and legalize through the destination country's embassy/consulate in Seoul. Select one path only; do not sequentialize both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Initial shareholders / managing member of KR_YUHANGHOESA; notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarize the Articles of Association and append MOFA Apostille. Consular Legalization path: notarize, obtain MOFA authentication, and have the destination embassy/consulate in Seoul issue consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are exclusive alternatives, not sequential steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A licensed Korean commercial bank (e.g., Shinhan Bank, Woori Bank, KEB Hana Bank or Korea Development Bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: if notarization of the bank reference letter is requested, have it notarized and then obtain MOFA Apostille. Consular Legalization path: have it notarized, MOFA-authenticated, and legalized by the destination state's embassy/consulate in Seoul. Use either Apostille or consular legalization according to the destination state's treaty status; never use both in one sequence.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before any incorporation step, every direct and indirect shareholder, director, executive officer, UBO, authorized signatory, and beneficial owner of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa must be screened against the consolidated OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, HM Treasury sanctions list, the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) designated person list, Korean government restrictive measures, INTERPOL Red Notices, and the World Bank debarment list. Enhanced due diligence must cover national and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates, adverse media, link to shell bank or high-risk jurisdiction, and inconsistent transaction purpose. A qualified AML officer must resolve all false positives before proceeding; monitoring and re-screening every 90 days are required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO), operated by the Supreme Court Commercial Registration System; name availability searches are also accepted at the district court registry of the intended jurisdiction.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name must be in Hangul under the Korean Commercial Act and the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Act. An English transliteration may be adopted as the foreign trade name, but the registered Hangul name controls for legal and banking purposes. The name must satisfy a four-tier structure: (1) distinctive trade-name element, (2) business-object description, (3) liability-type principle, and (4) the statutory suffix Yuhan Hoesa for the limited liability company. Phonetic transliteration from Hangul to Latin characters is required for the English trade-name alias. Any name containing a foreign word may require transliteration into Hangul to determine identical or confusingly similar conflicts.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the commercial registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant must obtain the written refusal notice and, within the statutory deadline for immediate appeal under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Act, file an objection with the head of the registry office that issued the refusal, attaching the refusal notice, the Hangul and English transliterated name, and any ministerial approval obtained for sensitive tokens. If the registry head maintains the refusal, the applicant must, without delay, file an immediate appeal to the competent district court; the appeal should identify identical or similarly registered trade names and establish the distinguishing element. The court's reversal enables resubmission. If the appeal is denied, the applicant must choose a new distinctive element, amend the Articles of Association draft and UBO documents, and pay the re-registration filing fee. Legal counsel should be engaged because these deadlines are materially shorter than general administrative litigation timelines.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office, commercial mailbox, or shared-lounge address is not permissible for this ISIC 3250 orthopedic-implant manufacturing entity. The National Tax Service (NTS) requires a physical domestic place of business for value-added tax registration and corporate income tax purposes; Korean commercial borrower banks require physical lease verification before opening a corporate account; and the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) requires a manufacturing facility with suitable cleanroom, electron-beam melting, and sterilization infrastructure as a prerequisite to the medical device manufacturing license. For this business, any virtual-office address will be rejected at the MFDS license stage and will result in refusal of the corporate bank account and VAT registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for physical inspection: (1) MFDS pre-license factory audit of cleanroom and electron-beam 3D printing facilities; 100% likelihood for high-risk porous titanium hip implant manufacturer. (2) MFDS unannounced surveillance inspection after license issuance; 70-85% probability within the first 24 months. (3) NTS field verification of the registered place of business during VAT registration or within the first tax period; 40-60% probability if the address is small or residential. (4) Municipal fire safety and building occupation inspection for commercial manufacturing use; 30-50% probability in the first year. (5) Labor inspectorate shakeup of workplace safety / chemical safety if manufacturing staff exceed threshold; 20-40% probability. These inspections justify retaining a physical leased facility and complete environmental and manufacturing safety documentation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Part V, Articles 543 through 568, especially Articles 544, 547, 553, 562, 564 and 565; Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act Articles 295 and 296; Foreign Investment Promotion Act Articles 2, 4, 5 and 8; Medical Devices Act Articles 6 and 26; Environmental Impact Assessment Act Articles 22, 37 and 43; Fire Services Act Articles 10 and 15.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court, Republic of Korea, and any district court registry having jurisdiction over the registered office of the company; filings may also be made electronically through the Supreme Court of Korea electronic registration system.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation; the final statutory instrument is the Certificate of Registered Matters (Corporate Registration Certificate) issued by the court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed by the Commercial Act. However, all subscription funds must be fully deposited into a blocked capital verification escrow account opened in the name of the company at a licensed domestic bank before the registration application is filed; the bank must issue a certificate of deposit verification confirming full receipt. If any subscriber is a non-resident, the remitted funds must enter Korea through a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, and the foreign-invested enterprise registration certificate or capital movement report must be obtained. The escrowed capital may not be released or used until the company is duly registered and the statutory officers provide post-registration instructions to the bank.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF KR YUHAN HOESA. At a duly convened meeting of the incorporators, founding directors, and persons designated to act as statutory officers of KR Yuhan Hoesa, a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) to be formed under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, held at the company's registered office in Seoul, Republic of Korea, on the date stated in the cover sheet, the chairperson confirmed that all participants had received lawful notice, that the meeting was duly quorate, and that each participant had the capacity to vote. After full and frank deliberation, the following resolutions were unanimously adopted and declared effective immediately. 1. ARTICLES AND INCORPORATION. RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation submitted to this meeting, having been executed by all incorporators, are approved in their entirety; that the company shall be constituted as a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea; and that the legal representative shall cause the application for registration of incorporation to be filed with the competent District Court Registry Office and shall execute all certificates, affidavits, and instruments necessary to complete statutory registration. 2. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION. RESOLVED, that the initial paid-in share capital of the company shall be the amount stated in the Articles of Incorporation, and that all issued membership units have been irrevocably subscribed and fully paid. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the subscription proceeds have been deposited into a restricted capital verification account opened at a licensed domestic bank, and that the bank's certificate of deposit verification, signed by the responsible bank officer, is attached to this resolution. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company shall be the Seoul address stated in the Articles of Incorporation, and that the lease agreement, landlord consent, and building use certificate are adopted and approved. 4. STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED, that the person named in the Articles of Incorporation is appointed representative director and chief executive officer, and that the person named in the Articles of Incorporation is appointed statutory auditor, each to serve until the next general meeting of members. RESOLVED FURTHER, that such officers shall have all powers necessary to open and operate bank accounts, appoint registered agents, appear before government agencies, and obtain all trade, customs, environmental, and medical-device manufacturing licenses. 5. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the representative director is authorized to open current and foreign-currency accounts with banks in the Republic of Korea; that the corporate seal and signatories listed in the account opening form are approved; and that all payment transmission by SWIFT wire and letter of credit shall require dual signatures as determined by the bank mandate. 6. UNIVERSAL AGENCY. RESOLVED, that any officer or attorney-in-fact may execute and deliver all documents, make all filings, and pay all fees necessary to give effect to these resolutions, including any variation required by the registry or licensing authorities, and that all actions taken in accordance with this resolution are ratified. This Pro-Forma First Board Resolution is legally binding on the company and each of its members. It was passed by unanimous written vote and signed by the chairperson and secretary on the effective date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Notarization and Execution of Articles of Incorporation and Subscription Instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public licensed by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Korea within the jurisdictional notarial office in Seoul, Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators shall prepare the Articles of Incorporation setting forth the company name, business purpose covering electron-beam three-dimensional melting manufacturing of porous titanium orthopedic hip joint prosthetics, registered office, issued capital, per-unit nominal value, names and signatures of subscribers, appointment of statutory officers, and absence of any restriction on foreign ownership. Each individual subscriber must appear before the notary with a valid passport or national identification card and a certificate of personal seal; corporate subscribers must provide a certificate of corporate seal and a power of attorney. The notary must verify legal capacity and identity, confirm that all signatories understand the document, and certify the Articles of Incorporation as a notarized deed. Any correction or annex must be initialed by all subscribers and included in the notarial record before filing.
required_dossiers: Notarized Korean-language Articles of Incorporation in original and notarial duplicate
Passport or national identification card of each incorporator
Certificate of personal seal or certified power of attorney for each subscriber
Certificate of corporate seal and board authorization if a corporate entity subscribes
Registered office lease agreement or title document and landlord consent
Certified identity and address evidence for each non-resident subscriber, apostilled if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses certification, the incorporators shall cure the irregularity identified in the refusal notice, furnish translated or apostilled proof of identity and authority, and resubmit the corrected deed; if refusal continues, application may be made to the competent Korean district court for a notarization order or the incorporation team may engage another licensed notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Direct Investment Notification and Capital Deposit Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: KOTRA One-Stop Foreign Investment Services Center and any designated foreign exchange bank in the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If any subscriber is a non-resident, the foreign direct investment notification must be filed through KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank before or immediately after the remittance of subscription funds. The foreign investor opens a temporary blocked account with the designated foreign exchange bank, remits the capital from abroad, obtains a foreign exchange purchase certificate, and then deposits the funds into the company's blocked capital verification account. The bank shall issue a certificate of deposit verification and, where applicable, a foreign-invested enterprise registration certificate. The funds must remain blocked and earmarked for the stated corporate purpose until the company is registered. KOTRA shall confirm any incentives and connect the company to tax and customs authorities where required.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Report form under Article 4 of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
Notarized Articles of Incorporation and business purpose description
Passport or nationality certificate of each foreign investor, apostilled if foreign
Corporate registration documents and board resolution if a foreign corporation subscribes
Share subscription statement and bank remittance advice
Certificate of personal seal and identification of the domestic legal representative
Power of attorney appointing the domestic representative
Capital deposit verification certificate issued by the designated bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the foreign investment report is returned or subjected to a deficiency notice, the investor and company secretary shall cure the deficiency within twenty days by supplying missing documents or correcting the remittance route; if the notification is rejected because the investment is below the statutory threshold, the parties may restructure the subscription or increase the capital contribution; KOTRA may assist in resolving bank and customs data mismatches.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Incorporation with the District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court, or the district court registry with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The representative director, through the company secretary or a licensed legal assistant, shall file the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa with the competent registry. The filing package must include the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital deposit verification certificate, subscriber statements, proof of lawful occupation of the registered office, and identification and seal certificates of the statutory officers. The registry officer will examine the application against the Commercial Act and court registration regulations, verify the payment of registration tax and local education tax, and, upon approval, issue the Certificate of Registered Matters. The registration date and registration number shall be stated on the certificate, after which the company acquires separate legal personality and may lawfully engage in business.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation in the court-prescribed form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of deposit verification from the Korean bank
Statement of subscription and payment schedule signed by all subscribers
Power of attorney appointing the filing agent and identification of that agent
Lease agreement, landlord consent and building use certificate for the registered office
Identification, resident proof and certificate of seal for the representative director and auditor
Receipt evidencing payment of registration tax, local education tax and court filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction or query notice, the company shall file supplementary documents within the period stated in the notice, usually two weeks; if registration is rejected, the company may refile after rectifying the irregularity or apply for adjudication under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act, and may appeal the registry decision to the competent appellate court within the statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration, Corporate Tax Registration and Factory Address Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office of the National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, through the Hometax electronic tax administration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after the issuance of the Certificate of Registered Matters, the representative director shall file business registration with the NTS through Hometax or in person at the local district tax office. The application shall state the corporate legal person, business purpose, corporate tax identification number, registered office, factory or manufacturing address, and the authorized representative. VAT registration is automatic upon business registration. If the company maintains a physical titanium implant manufacturing facility, the same business registration shall be linked to the factory address, and the company shall also register with the national employment insurance, national pension, health insurance and occupational safety authorities within the statutory deadlines. The NTS will issue a business registration certificate with the corporate taxpayer number, which is required for bank account activation, customs clearance, import of equipment and issuance of tax invoices.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registered Matters issued by the court registry
Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Business registration application form prescribed by the NTS
Lease agreement and building use certificate for the registered office and factory
Representative director identification and certificate of personal seal
Certificate of corporate seal and signature specimen
Bank account confirmation or proof of deposit account opening
Factory floor plan and site map if a manufacturing facility is established
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS queries or delays the business registration, the company shall respond through Hometax with corrected lease, building use or factory documents and pay any late-filing penalty; if the factory address registration is suspended, the company may obtain a temporary business license for the registered office and separately supplement the factory building approval before commencing production.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Medical Device Manufacturing Business License and Korean Good Manufacturing Practice (KGMP) Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), Medical Device Bureau, through its regional authority responsible for on-site inspection in Seoul or Gyeonggi Province
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing the manufacture of Class III porous titanium hip joint prosthetics, the company must obtain a Medical Device Manufacturing Business License under Article 6 of the Medical Devices Act. The application must demonstrate that the manufacturing facility, including electron-beam 3D melting equipment, acid etching passivation lines, ultrasonic cleaning rooms, packing areas and quality control laboratories, satisfies the physical, safety and quality requirements. After the license is granted, the company must apply for KGMP certification under Article 26 through an on-site inspection verifying the quality management system against ISO 13485 requirements. MFDS inspectors will review standard operating procedures, equipment calibration, validation protocols, personnel training, material traceability, cleaning validation and release testing. The license and KGMP certificate are prerequisites for future individual product technical file approvals and for lawful placing of the medical device on the market.
required_dossiers: Application for Medical Device Manufacturing Business License in the MFDS-prescribed form
Certificate of Corporate Registration and business registration certificate
Site plan, facility floor plan, cleanroom classification and air-handling system descriptions
Manufacturing quality manual and standard operating procedures for electron-beam melting and finishing
Equipment list and calibration or validation protocol for each production and testing machine
Draft Korean Good Manufacturing Practice (KGMP) quality system documentation aligned with ISO 13485
Environmental approval and fire safety certificates for the manufacturing premises
Certificate of corporate seal and representative director identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MFDS issues a deficiency letter, the company shall submit supplementary data within the stated period, normally thirty days; if the facility fails the on-site KGMP inspection, the company shall implement a corrective action plan, request reinspection, and preserve the manufacturing business license; denial of the license or certificate may be challenged through an administrative appeal to the Minister of MFDS and thereafter through administrative litigation within ninety days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Impact Assessment, Discharge Facility Registration and Fire and Civil Defense Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Environment (MOE) through the regional environmental office; National Fire Agency through the local fire station; and the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA) for workplace safety approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company shall complete the required environmental review or environmental impact assessment approval before installing production equipment, and shall register all air pollutant emitting facilities, wastewater discharge facilities and hazardous waste generators with the competent Korean environmental authorities. The titanium manufacturing process may generate metal particulate, acid wastewater from etching and passivation, degreasing VOCs, and titanium scrap or swarf, so a pollution prevention plan must be approved. The company must also obtain a Fire Safety Certificate from the local fire station for the manufacturing occupancy, demonstrate compliance with building fire resistance and evacuation requirements, and pass a structural load inspection confirming that the floor can support electron-beam melting equipment and vacuum furnaces. KOSHA clearance requires a workplace hazard analysis, chemical management plan, emergency response plan, exhaust ventilation design, and worker safety training program.
required_dossiers: Environmental impact assessment or prior environmental review decision letter from MOE
Air pollutant emitting facility and wastewater discharge facility registration forms
Pollution prevention plan and emission calculation sheets for VOCs and particulates
Hazardous chemicals inventory and safety data sheets for titanium, acids and solvents
Fire safety certificate application and building floor plan showing fire barriers and exits
Structural load inspection report for electron-beam and vacuum equipment
Waste generator registration for titanium swarf, etching solution and acidic sludge
Occupational safety and health management plan and emergency response plan
On-site inspection appointment request to the regional environmental office, fire department and KOSHA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the environmental approval is rejected, the company shall commission a licensed environmental consulting firm to conduct a supplemental environmental impact study and refile with the regional environmental office; if the fire safety certificate is withheld, the company shall cure the code violations, obtain temporary authorization if allowed, and schedule reinspection; if KOSHA identifies an unsafe condition, the company shall implement required engineering controls and PPE before obtaining the final workplace clearance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), Ministry of Environment (MOE), National Fire Agency, Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA), and the local municipal construction and factory administration office

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, acting through the district tax office with territorial jurisdiction over the domestic place of business, and using the HomeTax electronic portal (hometax.go.kr); for customs/export registration, the Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident person establishing or owning a Korean domestic Yuhan Hoesa must first complete incorporation under the Commercial Act at the competent Korean court registry, then file the statutory NTS business registration application, named the business registration (TIN/VAT ID) application under the Value-Added Tax Act, with the competent district tax office within 20 days from the date of business commencement. Documents include the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, domestic lease/office evidence, representative identification, foreign investment report under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act where applicable, and a written appointment of a domestic tax agent if the foreign entity has no residence or place of business in Korea. After review, NTS issues a 10-digit business registration number that simultaneously functions as the corporate income tax ID and VAT ID, requiring no separate VAT number. For export activities, the company must subsequently create its Korea Customs Service account and exporter registration in UNI-PASS and obtain the relevant medical device exporter/notifier registration from the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety if not already held.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (a Korean domestic Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation taxed under the Corporate Tax Act on its worldwide income, with no pass-through classification for Korean tax purposes).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box or any other pass-through-election for a domestic LLC. Qualifying domestic parent-subsidiary groups may elect the consolidated corporate tax regime under the Corporate Tax Act, but that election is an aggregation method and does not alter the entity-level classification of the Korean LLC.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold applies to companies; every business, including a domestic Yuhan Hoesa, must file business/VAT registration with the NTS from business commencement. Korean law provides a simplified taxpayer regime for certain individual natural-person businesses with annual taxable revenue not exceeding KRW 80,000,000, but a corporation cannot use that regime and must complete standard VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea mandates the issuance of electronic tax invoices (ETI) through the NTS HomeTax e-Tax Invoice system. There is no third-party pre-clearance or fiscal stamping engine; the anti-fraud architecture is based on mandatory NTS electronic transmission, invoice transaction matching, credit-card sales information reporting, cash receipt compulsory issuance in the service sector, and API-based e-Tax Invoice integration from taxpayer ERP systems. Export supplies must be evidenced through zero-rated ETIs and export customs clearance data submitted through KCS UNIPASS into the same NTS audit trail.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods that are physically exported from Korea and services supplied to foreign customers for credit or qualifying offshore use are subject to zero-rated VAT under the zero-rating provisions of the Value-Added Tax Act. The exporter must evidence actual customs clearance, legal exportation from Korea, transfer of title and risk to the overseas counter-party, and the receipt of foreign currency export proceeds. Input VAT incurred in manufacturing titanium orthopedic implants is creditable and refundable once the export zero-rating position is substantiated; additionally, the implants must be manufactured and exported in compliance with the Medical Devices Act.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (KCS UNI-PASS export clearance record, including export bill and manifest data)
Bill of lading or airway bill
Zero-rated VAT tax invoice issued through NTS HomeTax e-Tax Invoice service
Foreign-exchange inward remittance certificate (Korean remittance confirmation or foreign currency purchase certificate) and bank ledger evidencing receipt of export proceeds from abroad
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service and Korea Customs Service may jointly verify that export declarations, customs clearances, container/air cargo movements, and bank letters of credit or wire remittances are mutually consistent. If export proceeds are not received, or if documents are forged, incomplete, or received late, the permitted zero-rating is reversed and 10% VAT becomes assessable on the full export consideration, together with additional tax, statutory interest, and, in cases of fraudulent or aggravated non-disclosure, criminal referral. The company remains liable to substantiate the export chain for the statutory tax-assessment limitation period, and any refunded input VAT may be reclaimed with penalties where the export zero-rating is disallowed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK); the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) is the competent foreign-exchange authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; the Financial Services Commission (FSC) supervises financial institutions for existing FX and anti-money-laundering compliance obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a free-floating exchange rate with current-account convertibility for genuine trade, services, dividends, and royalties, but capital-account movements are conditional on declarative compliance rather than unrestricted. The KRW is not a fully convertible currency in the sense of unrestricted convertibility for any purpose; the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act requires that all resident cross-border transactions be supported by an underlying business purpose and be reported through a designated foreign-exchange bank to the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). An inbound direct investment is permitted without an individual central-bank license, but the investor must file a Foreign Investment Notification and the domestic bank must verify the receipt. Profit and dividend remittance is allowed if the foreign-invested company can prove origination from properly notified FDI, has settled corporate tax, and supplies a board resolution, audited financial statements, and a tax clearance certificate. The MOEF can impose prudential regulation, including leverage measures on FX derivatives and temporary convertibility restrictions during a balance-of-payments crisis. In practice, cash flows generated by the orthopedic implant company are freely convertible to KRW for current operating needs, and dividends can be repatriated through the domestic FX bank once the documentary trail is complete.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Goods exporters must collect foreign-currency proceeds within 15 months from the date of the export declaration and deposit them into a domestic Foreign-Currency Deposit Account at a designated foreign-exchange bank. The statutory mandatory conversion ratio is 0% under normal market conditions: the exporter may retain 100% of the proceeds in foreign currency or sell them for KRW at the market rate. Each receipt must be reported to the FEIS using the export declaration number and the relevant medical-device shipping documents. An extension of the 15-month settlement period may be requested through the designated bank if the exporter demonstrates a genuine collection delay, returned goods, or currency risk. During an emergency balance-of-payments disturbance, the MOEF may temporarily require full or partial surrender, but no emergency surrender regime is currently active.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Deposit Account; KRW Corporate Operating Account; Trade Settlement Account
Foreign-Currency Deposit Account for export proceeds; Basic Operational KRW Current Account
Capital Escrow Account for foreign direct investment receipt; General KRW Transaction Account
Basic Operational Currency Account; Letter-of-Credit and Import/Export Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low; offshore digital EMIs cannot serve as the primary treasury rail for a Korean-resident company because they are neither licensed banks nor electronic financial business operators under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. They cannot hold KRW current accounts, access Korea's won settlement systems, or file the FEIS declarations required for capital and trade flows. A foreign EMI may be used only as an ancillary treasury interface for upstream or downstream multi-currency collection, provided the final KRW settlement and statutory reporting occur through a domestic licensed bank. Relying on an offshore EMI for inbound FDI or the collection of export proceeds would invalidate the foreign investment notification, create an unlicensed banking arrangement, and produce an immediate regulatory and AML concern for the domestic bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory director(s) and any non-resident ultimate beneficial owner(s) must generally appear physically at the Korean branch to complete the real-name financial verification under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act. Remote consular proxy opening is not a statutory entitlement and is rarely accepted as a substitute for the first in-branch interview. An apostilled power of attorney may appoint a local account signatory, but the relevant director still needs to complete a face-to-face or bank-approved video-assisted identity verification before online banking is activated. We recommend budgeting two to three business days for the opening director to visit the bank with the original foreign investment registration, company articles, and individual passports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The beneficial ownership chain contains a non-resident corporate shareholder that was capitalized through a discretionary trust in a jurisdiction with weak tax-identifier disclosure, resulting in an unverifiable ultimate beneficial owner for the bank's customer due diligence framework.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete historical ownership map from the natural-person UBOs to the Korean entity; the trust deed, letter of wishes, and register of beneficiaries issued by the trust administrator; a beneficial-ownership declaration under the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information; certified passport copies and tax-residency certificates of every natural person holding at least 25%; a notarized memorandum explaining the commercial purpose of the intermediate holding layer; and a licensed Korean legal opinion validating the structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inward capital contribution is remitted from a pooled treasury account or a third-party related entity, not from the shareholder account named in the Foreign Investment Notification, which triggers a potential money-laundering doubt under FATF Recommendation 10 and a mismatch with the FEIS declaration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The signed share subscription agreement and board resolution approving the capital increase; the remitting entity's 12-month bank statements and formation documents; the remitting bank's attestation of account beneficiary and source of funds; audited group consolidated financial statements; the intra-group financing agreement explaining the payment route; and a sworn source-of-wealth statement supported by asset sale deeds, dividend vouchers, or liquidation records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The company is classified as a medical-device manufacturer under ISIC 3250 yet lacks a Korean MFDS manufacturing license at the time of the account opening, raising concerns about regulated business operations and potential proceeds from unapproved medical-device sales.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The MFDS medical-device manufacturing license, including the license for manufacturing and importing medical devices, and the KGMP certificate; ISO 13485 certificate; radiation-safety permits for the electron-beam facility; product registration certificates for titanium hip-joint prosthetics and orthopedic plates; documented MFDS applications for any pending products; and a corporate compliance certificate covering quality assurance, product liability, and recall procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The initial export letter of credit names a general trading company as the contract counterparty rather than a hospital or registered distributor, with the final hospital user absent, creating a red flag for possible over-invoicing or under-invoicing on high-value orthopedic implants.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The underlying distribution agreement with the trading company; the end-hospital purchase order or multi-year framework contract from the distributor; independent medical-device price benchmarking; a written Incoterms and commission fee explanation; prior LC and MT103 records from the trading company; customs declarations for the first shipment; and the final product HS code classification, such as 9021.31, with a price range corroborated by an independent auditor's trade-margin review.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder must file the Foreign Investment Notification under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act at the designated domestic foreign-exchange bank or through KOTRA before the remittance date. The capital must arrive by SWIFT MT103 from a bank account held in the investor's legal name, with the remittance reference clearly stating the foreign investment registration number and the FEIS purpose code for inbound direct investment. On arrival, the beneficiary bank credits the LLC's Foreign-Currency Deposit Account; if KRW is required for operations, the bank converts the funds at market rates and reports the foreign-exchange sale under FEIS. The bank verifies paid-in capital by matching MT103 field 50, the beneficiary account in field 59, the Foreign Investment Notification certificate, and the commercial registration documents. The company's Korean counsel then files the paid-in capital return with the court, and the bank's deposit certificate serves as the statutory capital verification evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For raw-material imports such as titanium powder and consumables, use SWIFT MT103 with the import declaration number, commercial invoice, packing list, and the exporter's beneficial bank details. For medium-risk medical-device export orders, use Commercial Letters of Credit advised through SWIFT MT700 or MT710, with conditions requiring presentation of the commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, certificate of origin, and MFDS conformity certificates. For repeat customers with established payment history, use Documentary Collections on D/P or D/A terms through the presenting bank, supported by MT400 transmissions or equivalent courier collection schedules. All outbound and inbound trade payments must be matched to the Korea Customs Service declaration and reported to the FEIS, and no trade disbursement should be routed to a third-party shell or freight-only intermediary without a documented procurement agreement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable KRW/USD forward foreign-exchange contracts for genuine export and import exposures, with tenors matching the underlying trade invoices
KRW/USD currency options and zero-cost collars executed through a licensed domestic FX bank using a real-demand hedge ratio
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for USD-denominated equipment finance related to the electron-beam melt facility

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for the Korean-resident entity as a primary hedge; any NDF usage is restricted to non-resident counterparties outside Korea and must not duplicate onshore hedge positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Attached Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 March of the year immediately following the fiscal year-end for a 31 December financial year; electronic filing with a certified tax accountant may extend the filing due date to 31 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Negligent underreporting penalty of 10% of the unpaid corporate tax; aggravated or fraudulent underreporting or failure to file penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax; overdue interest accrues at approximately 0.022% per day. Persistent non-compliance, including five consecutive years of dormant operations, may trigger court-ordered administrative strike-off from the commercial register under Article 520-2 of the Korean Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual External Audit Report Filed Through the Financial Supervisory Service DART System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) / DART Electronic Disclosure System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the fiscal year-end for entities subject to statutory external audit; audited financial statements must also be attached to the annual corporate tax return due by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to comply with the external audit filing requirement is subject to administrative corrective orders, fines, and regulatory sanctions under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies. Where the audited financial statements also support the corporate tax return, the NTS underreporting and overdue interest penalties set out above will apply, and sustained inactivity may lead to administrative strike-off of the company after five dormant years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Medical Device Manufacturing Business Annual Compliance Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) or the competent Regional Office of Food and Drug Safety
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for the preceding calendar year, or on the exact renewal date imposed by the MFDS manufacturing licence conditions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or non-filing may result in administrative fines, suspension of the medical device manufacturing business licence, or licence revocation under the Medical Devices Act. Continued cessation of licensed manufacturing activity can also support commercial register strike-off as a dormant company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any change in shareholding, paid-in capital, or beneficial ownership of a foreign-invested enterprise; the annual status report follows the foreign investment notification cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report foreign-investment changes may lead to denial or revocation of foreign-investment incentive benefits, administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and enhanced scrutiny by banks and the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit. Persistent failure to maintain active registration may contribute to dormant-company administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent CPA audit is required under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies where: (1) the entity is a listed or public-interest company; (2) total assets at the preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.0 million); or (3) the entity is designated by the Securities and Futures Commission or compelled by another statute, such as financial industry rules or MFDS licensing conditions. A Yuhan Hoesa LLC below these thresholds may not require a statutory external audit, but must still prepare annual financial statements supported by books and records for corporate tax purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) for entities subject to statutory external audit and for listed companies; K-GAAP / Korean Accounting Standards for non-listed small and medium enterprises. Manufacturing-specific inventory, impairment, and contingent liability measurement for medical devices also follows MFDS regulatory costing requirements and the applicable accounting standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not currently require a standalone public annual UBO confirmation filing for a privately held Yuhan Hoesa LLC. However, every transfer of member interests must be recorded in the Register of Members kept at the registered office and notified to the Korean commercial registry through the applicable amendment filing. Where the enterprise qualifies as foreign-invested, any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership must be reported to MOTIE/KOTRA within 30 days. Korean financial institutions will also require annual or event-driven confirmation of beneficial owners as part of customer due diligence under the Financial Transaction Reports Act.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% (2025 statutory rate) on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion, plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on national corporate tax payable, producing a combined top corporate rate of 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korea provides: (i) tax holidays for foreign investment zones allowing 100% corporate tax exemption for 5 years and 50% reduction for the next 2 years for qualifying high-tech projects; (ii) preferential free-zone income tax exemptions under the Special Cases of Taxation Act, including Jeju-type business models; (iii) patent box equivalent R&D cash credits and income-based R&D tax deductions (up to 30–40% of qualifying R&D investment); (iv) SME tax reductions and exemptions under the Tax Incentive Limitation Act; and (v) Korean investment tax credits for facility automation in medical device manufacturing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Return Statement (법인세과세표준및세액신고서) - NTS Form 10-1, filed electronically through HomeTax (홈택스)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with mandatory interim prepayment returns every six months
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year. For a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa: 31 March of the following year. Interim prepayment returns must be filed within 2 months after the first half of the fiscal year (for calendar-year taxpayer: 31 August). Non-resident payors of Korean-source income must file a Withholding Tax Return by the 10th day of the month following the month of payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number, company name, head office address, representative director, business code (ISIC 3250 / KAICU 21300: medical appliances manufacturing), fiscal year, number of non-resident shareholders and foreign-paid-in-capital ratio over 1%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must be disclosed. If any foreign shareholder holds at least 5% equity, the Korean LLC must attach an international transaction report (국제거래명세서) for related-party cross-border transactions. Do not leave blank when the Korean entity is a 100% foreign-owned subsidiary; understating shareholder disclosure can trigger penalty under the Act on the Coordination of International Tax Affairs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.failure_penalties: Late filing or omission: 20% of final corporate tax liability as negligent non-filing penalty; 40% if the omission is fraudulent; plus daily late-payment surcharge of 0.022% from the statutory deadline. Criminal tax fraud threshold is evading more than KRW 300 million, punishable up to 10 years' imprisonment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter total gross revenue from domestic and export sales of porous titanium orthopedic hip prosthetics, including invoiced amounts from the electron-beam 3D melting production facility. Sales discounts, returns, and allowances are deducted separately.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Sales to non-resident related distributors must be reported at arm's length. The comparable uncontrolled price (CUP) method is preferred for identical medical devices. For contracts with non-resident buyers, attach transfer pricing documentation if the aggregate cross-border related-party revenue exceeds KRW 5 billion. Under no circumstances may the taxpayer reclassify export sales as service fees to avoid the corporate tax assessed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs of raw titanium powder, 3D printer energy, direct labor, manufacturing overhead, physical wear allowance, and factory rent. Deductions are allowed if directly related to manufacture and supported by proper invoices.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to overseas related-party suppliers for medical-grade titanium powder or components must be supported by a formal procurement contract, customs declarations, and transfer pricing analysis if the purchase price exceeds arm's length range. Korean customs and tax authorities may recharacterize inflated import prices as disguised dividends or royalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as Box 2 minus Box 3. The gross margin for a medical device manufacturer typically runs 35% – 60%; an anomalous margin may trigger a tax audit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain a gross-margin benchmark study (e.g., under the TNMM) using Korean and regional orthopedic implant comparables. If the Korean LLC is a contract manufacturer for a foreign parent, the gross profit must leave an adequate functional reward for the routine intermediate manufacturing activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Selling, General and Administrative Expenses (SG&A)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Include salaries, rent, commissions, distribution fees, marketing, royalties, attorney and auditor fees, and R&D expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties paid to a non-resident licensor for patented implant surface technology must be reported gross and separately. You must verify that the payee is the beneficial owner and that a tax treaty rate reduction was approved. If no treaty application is filed, the payer must withhold 22% (20% national + 2% local) on the royalty gross amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 4 minus Box 5. This line reconciles to the management accounting statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the entity simultaneously operates an offshore e-commerce platform, an independent functional analysis is required. The operating income cannot be drained through management fees to a non-resident headquarters without substantive services actually provided in Korea.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, dividend income, FX gains/losses, disposal gains on fixed assets, and provisions recognized under Korean GAAP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-related interest paid (e.g., shareholder loan interest) must be reported with loan agreement details. Under the thin-capitalization rule in Korea, interest paid to a non-resident shareholder exceeding a 3:1 debt-to-equity ratio (or 6:1 in certain institutions) is not tax deductible and will be reclassified as constructive dividend, subject to 22% withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income per Korean GAAP financial statements based on the trial balance of the Yuhan Hoesa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The tax return must be prepared on the same basis as the audited financial statements. Common adjustment triggers include unrealized foreign exchange gains/losses or intra-group merger gains not yet recognized under the Corporate Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile fiscal depreciation (EEA: electron-beam 3D printers, CT scanners, sterile packaging equipment) with tax-depreciation limits set by the National Tax Service asset schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For equally depreciated equipment used for both local and export sales, no special non-resident restriction applies. However, imported second-hand machinery from a foreign related party must be depreciated on an arm's length acquisition cost. Accelerated depreciation must be documented under Article 39 of the Corporate Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entering expenses not deductible under Korean tax law: entertainment over statutory limits, personal expenses, unpaid income tax, donations exceeding limitations, fines and penalties, and unsubstantiated foreign invoices.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fee payments to a foreign advisory company with no actual economic activity in Korean residence (no office, no employees, no records) will be non-deductible, and the remittance will be additionally treated as unsupported outflow subject to 22% WHT. Prepare a foreign payment register and service-satisfaction evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 - Taxable Income before Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 8 + add-backs (Box 10) + depreciation adjustments − deductible deductions (Box 9) − other statutory deductions. This is the pre-NOL taxable amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prior-year losses attributable to a Korean branch of a non-resident are not automatically available to an LLC newly converted from a branch. NOL carryforward requires a formal carryforward schedule and approval basis; the NOL deduction may not exceed 80% of the income of a large corporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 - Net Operating Loss (NOL) Carryforward Deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the allowable loss carryforward from earlier tax years (maximum 10 years for losses incurred from fiscal years beginning after 1 Jan 2019).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The NOL deduction is only applicable to losses previously reported on valid corporate tax returns in Korea. Non-resident shareholders cannot cause the LLC to offload losses of a foreign parent to a Korean subsidiary. Tax authorities disallow cross-border NOL sharing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.failure_penalties: Claiming false NOL is subject to 40% additional tax under Article 47-2(1) of the Corporate Tax Act, plus criminal liability if intent is proven.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The final taxable base after the NOL deduction and all other adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean LLC with non-resident owners, this amount is the measure for corporate tax. It also serves as the denominator for the subsequent outbound distribution: after payment of corporate tax at box 14-16, the remaining after-tax profit can be remitted as dividends subject to acquiring shareholder withholding at 22% statutory (unless treaty reduced).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Graduated national corporate income tax on Box 13 as follows: up to KRW 200 million: 9%; over 200 million to 20 billion: 19%; over 20 billion to 300 billion: 21%; over 300 billion: 24%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where trade tax or foreign-sourced tax credits apply, they must be reported in the adjacent credit schedule. Non-resident shareholders cannot use corporate tax credits to offset their own dividend tax obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible credits: R&D tax credit, investment tax credit, foreign tax credit, employment tax credit, and special tax incentives for Free Economic Zones / Free Trade Zones.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: R&D tax credit for new implant coating technology is powerful — the Korean LLC should complete a technical report. If the foreign parent pays for the R&D and merely has the Korean subsidiary execute the research, the Korean subsidiary may not claim the credit; there must be actual research activity with Korean personnel and risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 16 - Total National Corporate Income Tax and Local Income Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sum of national corporate tax (Box 14 minus Box 15) and local income tax surcharge equal to 10% of national corporate tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Local income tax is computed automatically in HomeTax. Local income tax is a national tax at municipal level; no separate treaty limitation applies. Foreign shareholders cannot request a treaty rate reduction on the local income tax component.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 17 - Tax Paid through Interim Prepayment and Other Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deducted: interim prepayment paid in the year for the current fiscal year, corporate tax withheld at source, preliminary return payments, and bona-fide estimated tax deposits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident-owned companies, include the amounts of previously withheld Korean-source tax on bank interest and dividend income. Do not claim a foreign tax credit for taxes of a foreign jurisdiction unless it has been paid abroad and is creditable under Korean law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable after all credits and prepayments. If it indicates a refund, a corporate tax refund claim must be attached.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refunds due to non-resident shareholders do not become remittable abroad until all claims are verified by the NTS. Pending refund, no dividend flow. Refundable taxes due to treaty over-withholding on dividends require a refund petition within 3 years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Supplementary filing: Report of International Transactions (국제거래명세서), comprising sales, purchases, loans, guarantees, royalties, and service fees with foreign related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A separate Form is mandatory if the aggregate cross-border amount with foreign related parties exceeds KRW 500 million. The schedule must disclose the highest-tax-rate jurisdiction of each counterparty. Failure to submit this schedule means that the transfer-pricing documentation penalty applies automatically.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Corporations failing to file by 31 March are assessed an additional tax of 20% of the payable corporate tax (100% refund of excess-interest paid if not filed within 30 days after due). If the return is inaccurate but not fraudulent, the additional tax is 10%; if fraudulent, 40% of underpaid tax. Late payment accrues at 0.022% per day on the unpaid amount. Criminal evasion under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act (Article 3) carries imprisonment up to 5 years, or 10 years when the amount of evaded tax exceeds KRW 300 million. A director who submits a false return may be personally named as the violator and directly subjected to imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory withholding rate is 22% per dividend distribution to non-residents: 20% national withholding tax under Article 98-1(3) of the Corporate Tax Act plus 2% local income tax surcharge (10% of the national withholding). DTA relief may reduce the national component to treaty rates, but the local income tax is not reducible by treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: (1) The non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by its home tax authority and, if required, a Beneficial Ownership (BO) certificate. (2) The Korean payer (or the non-resident itself) must file a 'Request for Reduction or Exemption of Korean Withholding Tax under a Tax Treaty' (NTS Form) together with the TRC and BO statement before the withholding tax due date (the 10th day of the month following the payment). 3) The payer is then allowed to withhold the reduced treaty rate. 4) If the reduced-rate application is rejected or incomplete, the payer must withhold the statutory 22%. 5) A refund of the excess WHT can be claimed within 3 years. The Korean tax authority will refuse treaty benefits where the recipient is a mere conduit or does not satisfy economic substance requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 22% (20% national + 2% local); treaty rates commonly 0-15% depending on jurisdiction (e.g., Korea-U.S. 10% for industrial royalties; Korea-China 10%; Korea-Japan 10%). Interest: statutory 22% (20% + 2%); treaty rates generally 0-10% for arm's-length bank interest or 10-15% for other interest. Any payment of royalty or interest to a non-resident must be reported on a Korean withholding tin and the remitting bank must be furnished with a copy of the approved treaty-rate form before remitting.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5,000,000,000 (approximately USD 3.8 million) in aggregate cross-border related-party transactions for a fiscal year triggers mandatory preparation and, upon 45-day notice by the NTS, submission of the Local File and Master File. In addition, the Korean subsidiary is required to file a report of international transactions with foreign related parties if the aggregate amount exceeds KRW 500 million. Country-by-Country (CbC) reporting applies to MNE groups whose consolidated revenue exceeds the OECD threshold of EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Korean tax authority applies a substance-over-form principle in the Corporate Tax Act (Article 14) and an international anti-abuse rule in the Act on Coordination of International Tax Affairs (Articles 5 and 24). For a Korean medical-device manufacturing entity, the taxable profits must be commensurate with the core income-generating activities (CIGA) actually performed in Korea, including: quality control of titanium powder, operation of electron-beam 3D printers, sterilization, regulatory approval administration (MFDS), and post-market surveillance. If the Korean LLC merely carries title while the non-resident parent conducts all substantive CIGA, the NTS may reallocate profits to the Korean entity, deny treaty benefits, and assess financial penalties. The tax authority also examines whether a foreign intermediary holding the Korean company's shares has the personnel, discrete funding, and corporate substance to be considered the true beneficial owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The director and controlling shareholders invoice KRW 800 million for 'commission fees' to a paper company in a zero-tax jurisdiction for the purchase of titanium powder, but no actual powder is delivered; the Korean LLC overstates COGS, evading corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 3(1) of the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, evasion of corporate tax is punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years and/or a fine not exceeding KRW 50 million. Where the evaded tax exceeds KRW 300 million, the maximum imprisonment term becomes 10 years. Korean tax authorities will add a 40% additional tax on the fraudulent underpayment and cannot waive the impost.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The NTS pierces the corporate veil when the LLC is used as a pure device for tax fraud; the director and beneficial shareholder are personally liable for the unpaid corporate tax, penalties, and interest. Simultaneously, each director who signed the fraudulent tax return is subject to criminal sentencing as a direct co-principal. Once more than KRW 50 million of tax remains unpaid, the NTS publishes the individual's name and places a travel ban (blacklisting) on the director, blocking departure from the Republic of Korea until the debt is settled or a security is posted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Korean Tax on Outbound Royalties / Hidden Profit Remittances
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Yuhan Hoesa licenses an intellectual property patent from the non-resident parent at a 30% royalty rate, pays US$5 million, and fails to withhold any tax because the parent claims a treaty exemption, but no TRC or beneficial ownership documentation is filed with the NTS; alternatively, the royalty is 300% above arm's length.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 122-2 of the Corporate Tax Act and Article 47-5 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, the withholding agent is liable to pay the under-withheld 22% tax plus a 40% negligent additional tax on the unpaid portion, and daily late-payment penalties of 0.022% per day from the due date. In addition, the Korean tax authority must recalculate the deductible royalty and add back the excess above arm's length as a 22% taxable deemed dividend — destroying the company's loss carryforward claim. Criminal liability attaches under Article 11(2) of the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act: failure to withhold is punishable by imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine up to KRW 20 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Article 45(1) of the Basic Act for National Taxes, the director who is the person required to withhold and remit the tax is personally, jointly, and severally liable with the corporation for the unpaid withholding tax and penalties. The NTS may execute against the director's personal bank accounts, followed by a travel blacklist. If the director actively signed a fraudulent foreign-payment instrument, he will be prosecuted as a principal offender and may serve actual imprisonment of up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty Abuse and Shell Company Conduit for Dividend Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The ultimate Korean resident beneficial owner inserts a Hong Kong company with no employees, no office, and no activity into the ownership chain solely to collect dividends from the Korean LLC and invoke the Korea-Hong Kong DTA's reduced 5% dividend withholding rate, while the actual decision-makers and manufacturing operations remain in Korea. This is a classic 'director's misuse' of a tax treaty to reclassify Korean-source income as Hong Kong-sourced.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 24(1) of the Act on Coordination of International Tax Affairs denies the treaty benefit and recharacterizes the dividend as Korean source income. The NTS will impose the full 22% withholding tax (20% + 2% local income tax) on the dividend plus a 40% fraud penalty on the under-withheld amount. The company is also subjected to an immediate audit extension for all related party payments. If the arrangement is deemed concealment of taxable income, the director may be prosecuted under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, facing imprisonment up to 10 years when the amount evaded exceeds KRW 300 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The NTS pierces the corporate veil and treats the shell Hong Kong company as the inactive alter ego of the Korean director. The director becomes personally liable for the full corporate tax amount, the 40% additional tax, and interest. The director is also blacklisted: an international travel ban is registered, Korean border-control denies boarding, and all bank accounts and real estate are subject to attachment. In aggravated criminal cases, the director is criminally convicted of tax infidelity and ordered to serve a sentence of 5 to 10 years. This same doctrine applies to any non-resident director who uses the Korean LLC to funnel profits through a third-country conduit to avoid the Korean dividend withholding tax.
